title: the sages
hook: the third book opens in a clearing full of old ascetics, and the first thing they ask a prince in bark clothes is to be their king
carry: you are our king, protect us

segments.voice: Yesterday: a sandal on a throne. Bharata rules from Nandigrama as the sandals' servant, and the second book closed with Anasuya's gifts to Sita.

Aranya means forest, and the third book, the Aranya Kanda, is the book of the forest. The forest Rama walks into now is Dandaka, the great wild country south of everything he knows. It isn't empty. The first thing he sees, Valmiki says, is a ring of hermitages: little huts, fires burning for the daily offerings, grass laid out for rites, deer wandering without fear, birds everywhere. Old men and women with matted hair look up from their prayers, and come out to meet him.
screen: `ARANYA: THE FOREST.` → `DANDAKA, THE WILD SOUTH.` → `A RING OF HERMITAGES.`

segments.voice: The sages see Rama, Valmiki says, and can't stop looking at him: his build, his calm, his beauty, the bark clothes he wears like a king's robes. They bring fruit, roots and water, and give the travelers a hut to rest in. Then they say something surprising. You are our king. Whether you live in a city or a forest, you are still the king, and a king is the one who protects. We've given up the rod of punishment. We've given up anger. We live by our austerities, so we're like children in your care. Protect us. Notice what's happening. Rama has just been stripped of the crown in Ayodhya. His brother is ruling through a pair of sandals. And here, the first people he meets hand the title straight back to him. Not the palace or the throne, but the duty. The sages have chosen a life without weapons, and someone has to stand between them and the dark. Hold onto that request. Much of the forest book grows out of it: the battles, the promises, even the danger that will come to Sita. It starts here, with old people in a clearing asking a young man in bark clothes to be what he was born for.
screen: `THEY CAN'T STOP LOOKING.` · `YOU ARE OUR KING, CITY OR FOREST.` · `WE'VE GIVEN UP THE ROD.` · `PROTECT US.` · then, large: `THE CROWN COMES BACK AS A DUTY.`

segments.voice: Picture a clearing in a forest, small fires, quiet people, birds, and then someone in your own life who relies on you to stand between them and trouble. Breathe in steadiness and breathe out calm, with no need to solve anything for them right now.
The sages. The forest ascetics of Dandaka welcome Rama and ask him, king or not, to be their protector.
Your line: you are our king, protect us. City or forest, the title holds. See you tomorrow.

original.note: Sanskrit daṇḍakāraṇya: the forest (araṇya) of Daṇḍaka, the wild country where most of the third book happens.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama goes into the forest to be alone.
what it means: he walks into a forest full of hermits who need a protector.
what a scholar hears: Aranya 1 has the sages name Rama king and protector even in exile, and the theme of protecting the hermits runs through the whole book.

chat.says: Rama had lost his crown. Why did the forest sages call him their king?
options: To them a king is one who protects, city or forest, and they needed one.
They hadn't heard about the exile and thought he still ruled Ayodhya.
They wanted him to take over their hermitages and teach them the Vedas.
chat.meaning: The sages said that city or forest, Rama is still king, and a king protects. Having given up the rod, they asked for his protection.

Aranya Kanda.meaning: the Ramayana's third book, the book of the forest

Dandaka.meaning: the great wild forest of the south in the Ramayana

Valmiki.meaning: the poet-sage who composed the Ramayana

Ayodhya.meaning: Rama's home city, capital of the kingdom
